thread.title: 5 Top Tech-Stock Plays Get Boost From Apple's Earnings Blowout

author: NANCY GONDO
title: 5 Top Tech-Stock Plays Get Boost From Apple's Earnings Blowout
text:
Apple 's ( AAPL ) post-earnings gap up early Wednesday boosted shares of exchange traded funds with a sizable position in the iPhone maker.
X Apple soared 4% to a new high Wednesday, following the Cupertino, Calif.-based company's fiscal Q3 earnings report after the close Tuesday. It beat views on both the top and bottom lines . Heading into the report, shares were finding support at the 50-day moving average . Apple rushed past a 194.30 buy point of a flat base and was in buy range from the entry.
That lifted several ETFs that are topped by Apple. Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund ( XLK ), which held a 14% weighting in the stock as of Monday, retook its 50-day moving average. It slid below the support level during Monday's sell-off.
The $22.7 billion fund led the broader market with an 11.3% year-to-date gain through Monday's close. The S&P 500 is up 6% in the same period, according to Morningstar Inc. XLK also has outperformed over the longer haul, with average annual returns ahead of the S&P 500 over the past three, five, 10 and 15 years.
More Apple Ideas Vanguard Information Technology's ( VGT ) top holding as of June 30 was Apple, at 15% of assets. The $21 billion fund, which also regained its 50-day line on Wednesday, was up 13.2% year-to-date through Monday's close. Its average annual returns over the past three, five and 10 years were a respective 21.1%, 20.5% and 14.7%. The S&P 500's returns for those same periods: 12.3%, 13% and 10.5%.
IShares U.S. Technology ( IYW ), which owns a 16.5% stake in Apple, also recovered its 50-day line. The $4.1 billion fund tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Technology Index. Its 2018 return is 12.2% — and its average annual returns over the long term also outperform the S&P 500.
Other funds topped by Apple include:
Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), with $65.5 billion in assets, held an 11% stake. Fidelity MSCI Information Technology Index ( FTEC ), $2.2 billion, 14% in Apple.
